root_idea.summary: The root centers on smoke produced by fuel and extends by resemblance to clouded color, spoiled or corrupted condition, hostility, and troubled outward peace.
root_idea.development: The primary image is smoke rising from combustion. From it develop usages for smoke-tainted or dusky things, fumigation, internal corruption or rancor, and other states viewed as smoke-like or troubled.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The canonical Quranic noun دخان is a distinct public form.

senses.usage_conditions: In 41:11, the heaven is described as resembling smoke, an image associated with its lack of cohesion. The ordinary concrete sense is also supported in the Quranic occurrences.
A reported Quranic interpretation applies this figurative sense to the دخان passage, rather than taking the word as literal smoke.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a fire, to emit smoke; of smoke or dust, to rise, spread, or diffuse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used with fire, smoke, dust, and similar matter as its subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a fire, to become smoky or vehement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a fire whose combustion is spoiled and whose smoke is raised by the addition of fresh or green wood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of food or meat, to become infected with smoke and acquire its odor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of food while being roasted or cooked when smoke from the cooking vessel predominates over its flavor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wine or another beverage, to become altered for the worse in odor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of smoke-tainting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dusky or dingy, inclining to blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of plants and animals, as though they were overspread with smoke.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a nature or disposition, to become bad, corrupt, or wicked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from smoke-tainted or spoiled matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smoke, make smoky, or fumigate something or someone; to smoke out a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction includes applying smoke or fumigant to food, places, garments, or persons; in one reported use, smoke was used to kill people confined in a cave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of grain or seed-produce, to become hard and full in the grain while taking on a slight dusky color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fumigate oneself or use fumigation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person fumigating himself with a substance used as incense or fumigant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of grain or millet; also a single grain of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form with ـة can denote one individual grain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The appearance of conflict, faction, sedition, discord, or similar disturbance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun derived from the imagery of smoke or a troubled fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Alteration for the worse in intellect, religion, or the grounds of a person's claim to respect or honor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression for underlying or spreading corruption.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dusky or dingy coloration inclining to blackness; in a sword, a dark broad-side blackness or its wavy grain and streaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to animals, garments, and swords; the sword usage includes its variegated patterning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rancor, malevolence, malice, or spite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative inner quality associated with smoke or clouded appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Badness, corruptness, or wickedness of nature or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative character description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smoke-tainted, especially of cooked food or meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes food or meat that has acquired a predominant smoky odor during cooking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Altered for the worse in odor, of wine or another beverage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective for a beverage affected by an unpleasant change of smell.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad, corrupt, or wicked in nature or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction دَخِنُ الخُلُقِ for a person characterized by a corrupt disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Incense or another substance used for fumigation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used to fumigate houses, tents, chambers, clothes, and similar objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain bird whose color resembles that of a lark or a dust-colored bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical bird name; the reported color comparison varies among authorities or manuscripts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of sparrow or small bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bird name; the entry cross-references a related form دُخْنَان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely hot, of a day or night; of a night, also dusky or dingy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The heat is described as oppressive enough to take away the breath; the dusky-night sense is a parallel comparison with smoke.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the construction “a truce upon smoke,” an outward calm or truce that lacks reconciliation and conceals inner corruption or rancor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression for unstable or impure peace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the epithet “the two sons of smoke,” Ghani and Bahilah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The epithet refers to the reported smoking-out and killing of a party of people in a cave by the two tribes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Evil or mischief arising from an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which the arising of trouble is pictured as smoke rising.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tobacco.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or current application of the word, generally with a pronunciation differing from the classical form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firewood that produces smoke.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun naming smoke-producing fuel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad, corrupt, or wicked in nature or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in the construction خُلُقٌ دَاخِنٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chimney or hollow channel through which smoke passes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes apertures or channels made over frying pans, fireplaces, and bath furnaces; the plural is دَوَاخِن.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dusky or dingy, inclining to blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective applied especially to a ram and similar animals; its feminine is دَخْنَاء.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of smoke.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place characterized by or containing smoke.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel for fumigation or incense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fumigation vessel, comparable to a مجمرة; its plural is مَدَاخِن.

cautions: The word in 44:10 has the supplied contextual gloss “smoke,” while the lexical evidence also preserves a reported Quranic interpretation of the passage as dearth, drought, sterility, or hunger.
The historical Quran citation in the lexical evidence is not independently transcribed as a modern verse location; the example uses the independently supplied QAC occurrence 44:10.
